results.occurrenceRemarks: Introduced by Dongjiang raw water, the drinking water which the Hong Kong Government buy from Mainland China. Rating equal to "endangered" by China Species Red List (2004)

results.identificationRemarks: A few points: 1- Radoszkowskius oculatus is a synonym of Wallacidia oculata. This is one of the most common species in HK. It is a female. In Mutillidae, females are apterous and males all have wings 2- the shape of the thorax excludes Odontomutilla: front part as wide (or thereabout) than back part (dorsal view) = Trogaspidiini (Wallacidia sp, etc.); Front part of thorax wider than back part = Mutiliini (Odontomutilla spp. etc.) 3- The red femorae narrows it down to Wallacidia oculata (in HK) 4- Beware of ID's in Insecta Hongkongica...for Aculaeates alone, about 50% are incorrect! 5- It is unfortunate but we dont have reliable local resources for insect ID's
results.occurrenceRemarks: An old photo: I wrote at the time..... Insecta Hongkongica suggests this should be Radoszkowskius oculatus but another source suggests Odontomutilla uranioides Mickel (Mutillidae: Euphutinae: Odontomutillini). According to Insecta Hongkongica if it is R. oculatus then it is rare. This appears to be a female. This was taken on our coffee table on the sun terrace this morning.
